::: {.why}
The failure mode here is silence, not incorrectness, and the only way to fix it is to practise narrating while writing, which feels absurd until the first real screen.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Solve three problems in forty-five minutes while narrating, and state the complexity of each before writing it.
- Identify the point where you stopped talking, and what you were doing then.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [45 min]{.task-min} Forty-five minutes, three problems, narrating continuously and recording. State the approach and its complexity before writing anything, which is what interviewers ask for and what most candidates skip. Aim for working code over elegant code and say when you are choosing that.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Review the recording for silences longer than fifteen seconds, and note what you were doing in each. The usual cause is a bug, and the correct behaviour is to narrate the debugging rather than to go quiet, because the debugging is the part they most want to see.
:::
:::

:::
